title: Gomer Jones: The Man Who Followed Bud Wilkinson at Oklahoma
question: Who replaced Bud Wilkinson as Oklahoma's head football coach?
answer: Gomer Jones, Bud Wilkinson's longtime line coach, succeeded him in 1964 and coached two seasons, going 9-11-1. Jones was also OU's athletic director from 1964 until his death in 1971.
summary: Gomer Jones followed Bud Wilkinson as OU coach in 1964, went 9-11-1 in two seasons, and served as athletic director until 1971. Here is his story.
body: Following a legend is one of the hardest jobs in sports, and at Oklahoma that job fell to Gomer Jones. When Bud Wilkinson stepped away after the 1963 season, the Sooners turned to the man who had coached their linemen for all 17 years of the Wilkinson era, from 1947 through 1963.

Jones was a star in his own right. A center and linebacker at Ohio State from 1933 to 1935, he captained the Buckeyes and was a consensus All-American in 1935. As OU's line coach he developed 16 All-American linemen, a big reason Wilkinson's teams controlled the line of scrimmage for so long.

His head coaching run lasted two seasons. The 1964 team went 6-4-1, finished second in the Big Eight and played in the Gator Bowl, which it lost. The 1965 team slipped to 3-7. Jones then gave up the coaching job, finishing 9-11-1, but stayed on as athletic director, a post he had taken in 1964.

He remained OU's AD until March 1971, when he died in New York City while attending the National Invitation Tournament. In 1978 the College Football Hall of Fame inducted him for his playing days at Ohio State, making him a Hall of Famer who also served as an Oklahoma head coach.
